title: Redis-Compatible Multi-Tenant Cache
decision: Choose the sharding, replication, failover, and tenant-isolation architecture for a regional Redis-compatible cache.
audience: Platform engineers, service owners, security reviewers, and operations.
prompt: Write an HLD for a regional Redis-compatible cache used by several internal services. Compare managed and self-operated approaches, then recommend an architecture that satisfies the scenario constraints.
constraints: Treat 200000 GET operations per second and 30000 SET operations per second as scenario assumptions, not verified Redis benchmarks.
The target in-region p99 latency is 5 milliseconds.
The service target is 99.99 percent monthly availability across availability-zone loss.
Cached data may be reconstructed, but failover should lose no more than 60 seconds of acknowledged writes.
One tenant must not exhaust another tenant's memory, connections, or request capacity.

title: Collaborative Document Editing
decision: Choose the consistency and synchronization model for a multi-user document editor.
audience: Application engineers, storage engineers, product owners, and reliability reviewers.
prompt: Write an HLD comparing operational transformation and conflict-free replicated data types for a collaborative editor with offline clients.
constraints: A document may have 100 simultaneous editors.
Clients may remain offline for 24 hours.
The design must preserve an auditable edit history.
The first launch supports text and comments but not arbitrary embedded objects.

title: Object Storage Metadata Service
decision: Choose the partitioning, consistency, and recovery architecture for an object metadata control plane.
audience: Storage engineers, database specialists, and operations.
prompt: Write an HLD for the metadata plane of an object storage service, including namespace operations, listing, versioning, and regional recovery.
constraints: The namespace contains 10 billion objects as a scenario assumption.
Reads outnumber writes by 20 to 1.
Create-after-write must be strongly consistent within a region.
A regional disaster may require asynchronous recovery with an explicit recovery point objective.

title: Event-Driven Metrics Pipeline Trigger
decision: Decide whether to replace a cron trigger with event-driven execution and fund an HLD.
audience: Data platform maintainers and the engineering manager who owns the migration.
prompt: Write a technical one-pager proposing that a daily metrics pipeline move from cron scheduling to source-publication events.
constraints: The current cron starts at 02:00 UTC.
Source publication varies by up to 90 minutes.
Duplicate events are possible.
The first decision is direction and prototype scope, not implementation approval.

title: OpenTelemetry Log and Trace Correlation
decision: Decide whether to standardize service correlation identifiers through OpenTelemetry.
audience: Service owners, observability platform engineers, and on-call leads.
prompt: Write a technical one-pager proposing a common OpenTelemetry-based convention for correlating logs, metrics, and traces.
constraints: The organization operates services in three programming languages.
Existing log formats cannot all migrate in one release.
The proposal must retain compatibility during a staged adoption.
The next action should be a bounded pilot if the direction is accepted.

title: Payment Idempotency Component
decision: Specify the request contract, state machine, concurrency behavior, and recovery process for payment idempotency keys.
audience: Payment service implementers, code reviewers, and operations.
prompt: Write an LLD for an idempotency-key component that prevents duplicate payment creation across retries and concurrent requests.
constraints: Keys are scoped to merchant and operation.
A key remains authoritative for 24 hours.
Concurrent requests with the same key and different payloads must not both succeed.
The design must cover timeout after downstream payment creation but before the response is stored.

title: Distributed API Rate Limiter
decision: Specify the component contracts and consistency behavior for a shared token-bucket rate limiter.
audience: Gateway implementers, service owners, and reliability engineers.
prompt: Write an LLD for a distributed token-bucket limiter used by API gateways in three availability zones.
constraints: Limits may be defined per customer and operation.
Gateways must continue with a documented degraded policy during a limiter outage.
Configuration changes should become effective within one minute.
The design must cover clock skew, duplicate requests, and hot customers.

title: Notification Deduplication
decision: Specify the state, interfaces, and retry behavior that prevent duplicate customer notifications.
audience: Notification platform implementers and on-call engineers.
prompt: Write an LLD for deduplicating email and push notifications consumed from an at-least-once event stream.
constraints: A logical notification may arrive through several producer retries.
Deduplication state is retained for seven days.
The system must not silently discard a notification when its state store is unavailable.
The design must support replay for incident recovery.

title: Self-Service Preview Environments
decision: Decide whether self-service ephemeral preview environments create enough developer value to fund.
audience: Developer-experience leadership, finance, security, platform engineering, and support.
prompt: Write a PRFAQ for a service that creates an isolated preview environment for each code review.
constraints: The target customer is an application team that currently shares a long-lived integration environment.
The customer promise includes creation in under 15 minutes as a scenario target.
Environments expire automatically.
The FAQ must address cost allocation, secrets, production-data restrictions, quotas, and support.

title: Customer Data Export
decision: Decide whether a self-service export experience should be built and what customer promise it makes.
audience: Product, privacy, legal, security, operations, and engineering leadership.
prompt: Write a PRFAQ for a customer-facing service that packages account data for download.
constraints: The customer must verify identity before requesting an export.
Some source systems publish data asynchronously.
The download expires.
The FAQ must address completeness, timing, regional policy, support, and abuse.
